lesson.summary: The first close-idea run after pull request #586 did what the change claimed for a ticket with no parent idea: the write-access step passed for the owner, `close-idea.sh` read ticket #590 and closed nothing; the path that closes an idea has not run yet, and nothing needs doing.
lesson.detail: Pull request #586 added the `close-idea` workflow: on a closed ticket it runs `factory/scripts/trusted.sh` on the account that closed it, then `factory/scripts/close-idea.sh`, which closes the parent idea only when the ticket was its last open slice and otherwise says why it closed nothing. In run 44949492728 both changed steps succeeded: `trusted.sh` passed the sender `edmulraney`, and `close-idea.sh 590` printed "issue #590 is a slice of no idea: nothing was closed" and exited 0, which is the script's stated behaviour for a ticket with no parent. Neither reviewer left an assumption. This run did not exercise the branch that closes an idea, and I could not read ticket #590 from GitHub in this session to confirm independently that it has no parent; the log is the only evidence of that.

cost.amount: Nothing: the run succeeded with no agent session, 0 dollars and 0 turns.
